summary: Questions as partitions of the set of indices, after Groenendijk and Stokhof's dissertation. A question is an equivalence relation whose answers form a partition; inclusion of questions in both printed forms; a constituent question is the intersection of its whether-questions; and, as a bridge to InqB.v, whether-p is the polar question ?p on inhabited states.

sources.citation: Groenendijk, J. & Stokhof, M. (1984). Studies on the Semantics of Questions and the Pragmatics of Answers. Dissertation, University of Amsterdam.
sources.available: pp. 213-224 read; the corpus copy is a scan with an OCR text layer

theorems.name: question_is_partition
theorems.source_claim: Q1. (2) gives an equivalence, and by (1) p. 214 the answers of an equivalence form a partition: every index lies in its own answer, and two answers that overlap are the same.

theorems.name: whether_bipartition
theorems.source_claim: Q2. whether-p has two possible answers, p and not-p (p. 214), and whether-p and whether-not-p are the same question (p. 219).

theorems.name: meet_cells
theorems.source_claim: Q3. The intersection is again a question, and its answers are the intersections of the answers of the two.

theorems.name: entails_iff_cells
theorems.source_claim: Q4. The two forms of (7) agree.

theorems.name: inclusion_facts
theorems.source_claim: Q5. (8): every question is included in the one-cell partition. (9): the partition into singletons is included in every question. (10): an intersection is included in its first term. (11): Q is included in R iff their intersection is Q.

theorems.name: who_from_whether
theorems.source_claim: Q6. p. 220: a constituent question can be constructed by intersection from the questions whether a G's, one for each a.

theorems.name: offers_monotone
theorems.source_claim: Q7. If Q is included in R, an information set that offers an answer to Q offers an answer to R. This is inclusion read as answerhood (p. 221: every answer to Q implies an answer to R).

theorems.name: cell_counts
theorems.source_claim: whether-p makes a bipartition; the constituent question a four-fold one (p. 215: n is the number of possible denotations of the predicate).

theorems.name: who_entails_whether
theorems.source_claim: The constituent question includes each of its whether-questions.

theorems.name: whether_does_not_entail_who
theorems.source_claim: Separating example 1: the converse inclusion fails.

theorems.name: independent_questions
theorems.source_claim: Separating example 2: two independent whether-questions; neither is included in the other.

theorems.name: information_and_answers
theorems.source_claim: Separating example 3: the information that p offers an answer to whether-p and not to the constituent question.
